Do you hear that? The constant gunfire? The shelling? And they tell the world there is a ceasefire? There is no pause. No reprieve. No safety for Palestinians in Gaza. On October 11, our team visited families whose tents had been burned, leaving them without shelter once again. Even as we filmed, heavy gunfire echoed around us. This is the reality of life in Gaza. Families who have lost everything continue to live under the threat of violence, yet refuse to be driven from their land. This is what steadfastness looks like. Sumud. A determination that is difficult to comprehend unless you understand what it means to face the loss of your homeland. They have burned their shelters, destroyed their neighborhoods, and displaced them again and again. But they have not broken their connection to Palestine. They are not leaving. They are not surrendering their right to exist on their land. Help support them. The Sameer Project is one of the only organizations that delivers aid in these danger zones. If authentic, it would be deeply disturbing and would raise serious moral and legal questions. War should never strip people of their humanity. Every civilian death is a tragedy, and any act that degrades the dead or celebrates suffering deserves careful scrutiny and accountability. In conflicts like this, emotions run high, but facts matter. Allegations should be investigated thoroughly, and those responsible for any war crimes or abuses should be held accountable, regardless of who they are. The world cannot become numb to human suffering. Justice should never depend on nationality, religion, or politics. Your donations are facilitating Palestinians going to work in Gaza. The transport initiative provides agency and mobility to people, which is crucial during these times. The Sameer Project provides 9 buses daily and transports on average 1,500 people everyday. The buses connect North Gaza with Gaza City and Gaza City with South Gaza. It is important to understand that many vehicles in Gaza have been bombed and the ones still running are barely functioning. No spare parts are allowed into Gaza and the buses we run are constantly breaking down. So having access to transport is huge for Palestinians in Gaza. Support this initiative through the General Fund.
